extracted.intended_audience: SEC staff, exchange legal/finance teams, market participants and Members of options exchanges
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evidentiary standards an exchange should follow when proposing or defending non-transaction fees (here, connectivity and port fees), including cost allocation, transparency, competitive effects, and operational justification. Focused on preparing an SEC Rule 19b-4 style filing to justify fee changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory fee standards (Section 6(b) of the Exchange Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exchange fees must be reasonable and equitably allocated, not designed to permit unfair discrimination, and not impose a burden on competition not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The filing should explicitly address how the proposed fees meet these statutory requirements; use quantitative and qualitative analysis to show reasonableness, equitable allocation, and no unfair discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: High standards of transparency for fee changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Exchanges, in setting fees of all types, should meet very high standards of transparency to demonstrate why each new fee or fee increase meets the Exchange Act requirements that fees be reasonable, equitably allocated, not unfairly discriminatory, and not create an undue burden on competition among members and markets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear, comprehensive explanation of methodologies, inputs, and rationale; disclose cost studies, allocation rules, and supporting data in the filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees should be based on costs and reasonable business needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Each exchange should take extra care to be able to demonstrate that these fees are based on its costs and reasonable business needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include an aggregate-cost analysis tying proposed fees to the exchange's costs of providing the service; show how fees cover costs and the basis for any margin/profit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess and disclose impact on Members including smaller Members
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the impact on Members—both generally and in relation to other Members, i.e., to assure the fee will not create a financial burden on any participant and will not have an undue impact in particular on smaller Members and competition among Members in general.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide analysis showing distributional effects across member types, and explain why the fee structure does not disproportionately harm specific participant classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding double-counting in cost allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that no cost would be allocated twice or double-counted between the Exchange and its affiliated markets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe allocation steps and checks used to prevent double-counting; reconcile with Form 1 filings and affiliate cost allocations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate allocation of total costs to each market (market-level allocation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the total cost for the Exchange and the affiliated markets for each cost driver as part of a company-wide budget process rather than simply dividing total cost evenly among marketplaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use bottom-up budgets from department heads, consolidate with Finance, and obtain senior management and board review/approval; explain allocation drivers (server counts, platform architecture, number of connections, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation methodology among core services
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine what portion of the cost allocated to the Exchange is to be allocated to each core service, e.g., connectivity and ports, market data, and transaction services, using thoughtful and consistently applied principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain rules used to allocate each cost driver to services (e.g., data center costs allocated more to connectivity), provide percentages, and show that methodology is consistently applied over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed line-item cost disclosure and percentages
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a detailed chart of line-item costs considered related to offering the service (e.g., Human Resources, Connectivity external fees, Internet services, Data Center, Hardware/software maintenance, Depreciation, Shared expenses), with allocated annual/monthly costs and % of all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include numeric breakdowns and explain rounding/derivation (annual to monthly conversion), and provide narrative detail on what each line item includes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human resources cost allocation procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Allocate personnel costs by identifying employees who perform functions related to the service, and then allocate percentage of each employee's time to the service (e.g., twice-yearly manager assessments, 100% allocation across markets, buckets for network connectivity/ports/market data).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document the process (manager consultations, time percentages, blended compensation rates), show sample allocations (e.g., 48.5% to 10Gb ULL connectivity for certain teams), and explain inclusion/exclusion rules for senior executives and ancillary staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justify operational necessity for technical changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Operational justifications for changes (e.g., bifurcation of the 10Gb ULL network) must be shown — such as capacity constraints, limited port availability, latency-sensitive member behavior, and infeasibility of simply adding switches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide technical explanation and evidence (usage patterns, member behavior, port headroom analysis) that alternative technical remedies would not adequately address the problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate member notice and transition planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide evidence that market participants were given adequate notice and time to prepare for network or fee changes (e.g., announcement date and effective date to allow migration or contract changes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include timeline of communications with subscribers, outcomes of subscriber discussions, and any negotiated accommodations or observed subscriber responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate competitive constraints and available alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that proposed fees are constrained by competitive forces and that market participants have alternatives (e.g., connecting to other options markets, using third-party resellers, sponsored access, or relying on another member's connectivity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present membership/connectivity data, examples of third-party resellers, evidence of member disconnections or choices (e.g., a market maker terminating membership), and explain how these options limit pricing power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of member demand and usage evidence to support fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Use evidence of member demand (subscription counts, net increases/decreases, usage behavior) and member feedback to support that members derive value from the service and to quantify fee impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide pre/post-change subscription counts, net changes, and qualitative subscriber feedback to demonstrate immaterial or material effects of the change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency over time and explanation for allocation changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply the same rules and principles year-to-year for cost allocation and explain minor shifts in allocation percentages when they occur (e.g., changes due to headcount shifts or product usage differences).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document what changed between years, give reasons (new hires, hardware refresh, usage shifts), and show that methodology remains consistent even if percentages shift slightly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconcile cost allocations across affiliates and filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain and reconcile differences in allocation percentages and methodologies between the Exchange and its affiliated markets and in prior similar filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide rationale for deviations (unique marketplace factors), reference affiliate filings (e.g., MIAX, MIAX Emerald) and demonstrate that allocations are based on marketplace-specific projections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate that proposed fees enable covering costs and modest profit
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that proposed fees (e.g., $13,500 per month per physical 10Gb ULL connection) are necessary to cover aggregate costs of providing connectivity and ports and to permit a modest profit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present the aggregate annual/monthly cost totals, proposed fee schedules, and simple revenue-to-cost comparisons illustrating coverage of costs and expected margins.
